groups.title: Pronominal NNC foundation
groups.proposal: Treat entitive and quantitive pronominal forms as absolutive NNCs and keep internal stem pluralization separate from subject number.
groups.writingJob: Build the typed pronominal NNC family, reject possessive State, and distinguish internal plural n from the following subject-number dyad.
groups.readingJob: Explain English pronoun translations without replacing the Nahuatl NNC structure with English pronoun structure.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the pronominal source and subject; the application enforces absolutive State and supplies only licensed plural structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Subject, and Number; do not add a State or plural-connector control.

groups.title: Simple personal-pronominal NNCs
groups.proposal: Build simple personal forms with the subject-conditioned eh or yeh stem and preserve their personal and nonanimate readings.
groups.writingJob: Select eh generally and yeh for the licensed third-person coordinates, then build the exact singular, common, or plural Result.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through personal, nonanimate, rare plural, and adverbial-collocation interpretations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the simple personal source and subject; the application selects the conditioned stem shape and realizes the Result.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add an eh-versus-yeh control; show the automatic selection as a clickable cue.

groups.title: Compound personal-pronominal NNCs
groups.proposal: Build compound personal forms with conditioned eh-huā or yeh-huā, internal plural n, licensed subject connectors, and distributive common-number stems.
groups.writingJob: Select the conditioned compound stem, add internal plural n where required, supply the licensed subject-number dyad, and build distributive eh-eh-huā or yeh-yeh-huā when intended.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through singular, common, plural, definite, indefinite, and distributive interpretations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the compound source, subject, and genuine distributive meaning; the application chooses stem shape, internal n, and subject connector.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Subject, and the existing genuine stem-relation choice; do not expose derived connectors.

groups.title: Compound personal variants and special contexts
groups.proposal: Preserve sounded and silent compound variants, modifier uses, and the first-plural doubled-person construction.
groups.writingJob: Build each licensed number variant and restrict doubled first plural to its exact personal context.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through variant equality, modifier meanings, and people-group interpretations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a genuine variant or contextual meaning; the application enforces its subject and structure restrictions.
groups.controlPolicy: Expose only genuine variant and doubled-first-plural choices when structurally available.

groups.title: What-interrogative pronominal NNCs
groups.proposal: Build tl-eh interrogatives across their licensed persons and distinguish fused elliptical in from a separate dependent-clause introducer.
groups.writingJob: Build tl-eh, its licensed person-number forms, its in fusions, and its clause-position interpretation.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through entity identification, fusion, and loss of interrogative force.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended clause relation; the application selects fusion, separation, and interrogative force.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse sentence and clause controls; do not expose spelling fusion as a separate grammar choice.

groups.title: Compound what, which, and who interrogatives
groups.proposal: Build tl-eh-huā, cā compounds, and āc with their exact person, polarity, fusion, and clause-position restrictions.
groups.writingJob: Compose the typed interrogative source, restrict āc to third singular, produce ayāc under negation, and apply licensed in fusion or separation.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through entity, selection, person, negative, and noninitial meanings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses source, polarity, and clause meaning; the application enforces person and realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Subject, Polarity, and clause controls; do not add derived form controls.

groups.title: Demonstrative and indefinite pronominal NNCs
groups.proposal: Build demonstrative īn and ōn and indefinite ah compounds with their fixed number and human-use restrictions.
groups.writingJob: Build typed demonstrative and indefinite sources, preserve silent demonstrative plural structure, apply the ah boundary rule, and gate special human itlah use.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through demonstrative reference, indefinite human or nonhuman meaning, and traditional spelling.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses source and intended special human meaning; the application supplies number and boundary realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Expose special human use only where it changes meaning; do not expose derived spelling or number carriers.

groups.title: Quantitive source system
groups.proposal: Build typed quantitive embed-matrix sources and their plain, interrogative, distributive, and clause-conditioned forms.
groups.writingJob: Analyze and compose licensed quantitive sources, choose the long matrix before internal n, and apply interrogative position conditions.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through quantity, extent, distributive, adverbial, and noninitial interpretations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user enters or selects a quantitive source and intended meaning; the application analyzes its structure and realizes it.

groups.title: Quantitive plural pattern, many, and some
